proposals.title: Graph-Based Spatial Domain Segmentation
proposals.summary: This analysis will construct a weighted graph where each node corresponds to a spatial spot and edges represent spatial proximity and gene expression similarity. The method will utilize graph clustering techniques to segment the tissue into biologically meaningful regions, ensuring that boundaries reflect gradual transitions and sharp changes. Special attention will be given to preserve expression patterns near region borders by avoiding over-smoothing and by incorporating local neighborhood information into the clustering algorithm.

proposals.title: Edge-Preserving Smoothing for Spatial Transcriptomics
proposals.summary: To address the challenge of sparse expression data without crossing true biological boundaries, this analysis uses edge-preserving smoothing algorithms such as bilateral filters or anisotropic diffusion. The approach will adapt smoothing parameters based on local intensity and spatial discontinuity, enabling improved denoising of the transcriptomics signals while retaining sharp domain borders. The performance will be evaluated based on the preservation of known tissue gradients and boundaries.

proposals.title: Integrative Dimensionality Reduction with Spatial Constraints
proposals.summary: This analysis aims to develop a low-dimensional representation that jointly captures gene expression variability and spatial relationships. Techniques like spatially-aware principal component analysis or autoencoders will be used, where neighborhood information is embedded into the dimensionality reduction process. The resulting features will be assessed for their ability to reveal coherent tissue regions, maintain boundary continuity, and provide clear separation of sub-regions even in the presence of measurement noise.

proposals.title: 3D Reconstruction Across Consecutive Tissue Sections
proposals.summary: In this analysis, spatial transcriptomics data collected from consecutive tissue sections will be aligned and integrated to reconstruct a three-dimensional tissue architecture. Section-specific effects will be corrected by using registration techniques and cross-section normalization. The 3D model will allow the study of continuity of expression domains and domain transitions across layers, providing insights into the gradual or abrupt changes in tissue organization.

proposals.title: Spatial Boundary Gradient Analysis
proposals.summary: This analysis focuses on the characterization of the regions near tissue boundaries where expression gradients occur. By leveraging spatial transcriptomic profiles, the method will quantify gradient steepness and identify transitional zones. A combination of curve fitting and differential expression analysis will help elucidate the gene expression changes occurring at the interfaces, thereby shedding light on both gradual and abrupt domain transitions.

proposals.title: Cell Mixture Deconvolution in Spatially Heterogeneous Regions
proposals.summary: Given the presence of mixed cell types particularly near domain boundaries, this analysis will apply deconvolution techniques to break down composite expression profiles into constituent cell types. Spatially informed deconvolution algorithms will incorporate both gene expression signatures and proximity information to assign cellular mixtures accurately. The outcome will improve boundary detection and tissue segmentation by distinguishing overlapping cell populations.

proposals.title: Resolution Sensitivity and Domain Robustness Assessment
proposals.summary: This study will systematically evaluate how changes in spatial resolution and sequencing depth affect the identification of tissue domains. Using both downsampled and high-resolution datasets, the analysis will assess the stability of domain segmentation results. The approach will help determine optimal resolutions and smoothing parameters that balance noise reduction with the preservation of sharp expression boundaries.

proposals.title: Spatial Neighborhood Denoising for Sparse Transcriptomic Data
proposals.summary: This analysis focuses on mitigating the impact of sparsity in expression data by leveraging information from immediate spatial neighbors. Advanced imputation techniques and local aggregation methods will be applied to enhance signal recovery without overly blurring domain boundaries. The approach will be benchmarked using both simulated sparse data and real datasets to ensure that the spatial context is effectively utilized while retaining biological variability.

proposals.title: Multi-Modal Integration of Spatial Omics Data
proposals.summary: In this analysis, spatial transcriptomics data will be combined with other spatially-resolved modalities (e.g., proteomics or metabolomics) to achieve a comprehensive view of tissue architecture. Using joint analytical frameworks such as graph convolutional networks or multi-modal integration algorithms, the method will co-learn from diverse data types while preserving spatial information. This integrated approach aims to enhance domain identification accuracy, improve cross-section integration, and provide richer biological insights.
